_comment: Church-specific language data, kept OUT of the source tree (S2 + S7).
Three things live here, because all are per-congregation and none belongs in
code that is published:
properNouns        - names and abbreviations the translator must keep verbatim.
Injected into the GPT prompt for the target languages whose
rule block carries that instruction - 10 of the 12 today;
Polish and one other have never had it.
glossaryTerms      - extra glossary records merged on top of theologicalGlossary.json.
Same shape as the entries there: category, context, translations.
glossaryCategories - descriptions for categories introduced above. getCategories()
merges them, so a category used by a record but described
nowhere would show up unnamed.
VALIDATED ON LOAD. An absent file is fine - the base glossary works on its own.
A file that EXISTS but is malformed is a hard startup error, not a silent empty
configuration: a broken file would otherwise serve every congregation without its
names and terms while looking healthy.
The real file is created per deployment and never committed - see .gitignore.
Point CHURCH_DATA_PATH at it, or drop it next to this example as churchData.json.
Keys are church ids as used in churches.json. 'default' applies to any church
with no entry of its own.

Beispielperson.context: Example of a congregation-specific term: a person or role name
